episode_title: OpenAI’s Head of ChatGPT: We’re entering a new era of AI (again) | Tibo Sottiaux
description_html:
Tibo Sottiaux leads ChatGPT and Codex at OpenAI. Under his stewardship, OpenAI has shipped some of its most consequential consumer launches: Codex, ChatGPT Work, and most recently, the new Dots personal agent platform. He joined me at DevDay, hours after his team launched more than 20 new products, to talk about where things are heading.

We discuss:

1. Dots, OpenAI’s new personal AI assistant

2. Why most actions on the internet will soon be taken by agents

3. Why loops, graphs, and fine-tuning agent workflows are a passing phase

4. Which skills are trending up and down in the AI era

5. How Tibo’s Dot warned him about a production outage five minutes before the launch

6. OpenAI’s approach to AI safety

summary.overview: Lenny Rachitsky speaks with Tibo Sottiaux of OpenAI about how agents, persistent memory, multimodal interfaces, and faster models could reshape software and work. Tibo discusses OpenAI’s Dots vision, the merging of Codex and ChatGPT, an open plugin ecosystem, safety investments, hiring, company culture, and why he expects the majority of internet actions eventually to be taken by agents.

takeaways.heading: Persistent active intelligence
takeaways.detail: Tibo’s vision is an intelligence that understands a user’s goals and preferences, learns from feedback, and is available across clients and devices rather than being tied to a laptop or phone. Dots is one expression of that vision, but he frames the broader goal as making technology work around people.

takeaways.heading: From loops to learning
takeaways.detail: Tibo thinks users will move away from manually designing loops and graphs. Instead, they will want an agent that learns what they are trying to achieve and improves through feedback without requiring detailed configuration.

takeaways.heading: Teams of agents
takeaways.detail: He alternates between running larger teams of agents and relying on a single larger agent as models improve. Faster models such as UltraFast help him stay in a creative flow, while future breakthroughs may allow one agent to keep more context and handle work previously divided among several agents.

takeaways.heading: Dots and ChatGPT
takeaways.detail: OpenAI plans to reduce the distinction between Codex, ChatGPT Work, and consumer ChatGPT, eventually bringing Dots’ capabilities into ChatGPT. Dots currently avoids model pickers and configuration; users mainly choose which channels they want to use.

takeaways.heading: Multimodal work
takeaways.detail: Tibo expects voice, multimodal inputs and outputs, shared whiteboards, and collaboration between humans and agents to move beyond today’s conversation-based interfaces. He says the technology is still clunky, but believes it will eventually feel as natural as talking to another person.

takeaways.heading: Multiple specialist Dots
takeaways.detail: Users initially get one primary Dot that learns their preferences deeply. OpenAI plans to let users create additional Dots with specific roles, such as monitoring Twitter, forming a virtual team with specialized responsibilities and extra guardrails where needed.

takeaways.heading: Open ecosystem
takeaways.detail: Tibo describes the ecosystem as a likely sleeper hit, citing 16 partners using Sign in with ChatGPT and plans for plugin extensions and discovery. Plugins will be recommended based on quality, usage, and retention rather than only marketing or keyword tactics, and popular plugins will participate in revenue sharing.

takeaways.heading: Research behind Dots
takeaways.detail: OpenAI has worked for more than two years on long-horizon tasks and coherent memory systems. Dots combines that research with the Codex harness, 24/7 operation, proactive behavior, and additional safety and security work; specialist Dots can run with monitoring, guardrails, and separate hardware.

takeaways.heading: Work keeps changing
takeaways.detail: Tibo does not expect work to settle into a stable form over the next few years. He anticipates radical change as voice and multimodal systems become less awkward, while also hoping AI will reduce meetings, noise, and pressure to do more rather than simply increase the number of prompts and tasks.

takeaways.heading: Human value and hiring
takeaways.detail: He believes human taste, creativity, learning, collaboration, and the desire to build meaningful things will remain important. Typing quickly is becoming less valuable, while connecting with users and knowing what good looks like matter more; he also sees roles blurring and says OpenAI has more than 120 former YC founders.

takeaways.heading: Advice for new grads
takeaways.detail: Tibo points to Ahmed Ibrahim, whom he describes as kind, collaborative, self-effacing, exceptionally fast-learning, and willing to use new technology aggressively. He credits those qualities with helping Ahmed progress from new graduate to a trusted leader of major OpenAI responsibilities.

takeaways.heading: OpenAI’s culture
takeaways.detail: He describes OpenAI as a bottoms-up environment where small groups can hack on ideas, gain momentum, and ship them while maintaining a high quality bar. People receive substantial autonomy and are expected to own mistakes, fix them quickly, and learn from them; Tibo says he has also caused outages, including taking production down on his third day.

takeaways.heading: Agents and the internet
takeaways.detail: Tibo thinks people are underestimating how quickly models will become cheaper and faster, how seamlessly modalities will combine, and how most internet actions may eventually be taken by agents. Products built for agents will need to handle much greater scale and rethink their economics, while human-facing multimodal experiences remain underinvested.

takeaways.heading: Safety and alignment
takeaways.detail: Tibo says OpenAI is investing heavily in alignment, security, guardrails, and secondary monitoring that watches primary agents for risky actions or prompt injection. He expresses confidence in the approach, noting that OpenAI chose not to release a more capable model, 6.1 Astra, and does not want to gamble with products used by more than a billion people.

takeaways.heading: The app’s complexity
takeaways.detail: Tibo’s main frustration is that models are close to making the application disappear but are not there yet. He wants to eliminate fatigue around model pickers, reasoning settings, and choices such as multi-agent versus Ultra, rather than requiring users to understand the underlying configuration.
